harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as the DHCP server on the private network (eth1, 10.50.50.0/24, static IP 10.50.50.254) shared with node2/node3, and confirmed node2 and node3 (enp8s0, already set to ipv4.method=auto rather than static) obtain their addresses dynamically from node1 (leases 10.50.50.101 and 10.50.50.100 respectively). Verified inter-node connectivity across the private network, then completed the mandatory one-node-at-a-time restart protocol for all three nodes, confirming changed boot IDs and full recovery of the DHCP server and client leases after each reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected topology: node1 (VyOS) has eth0 (default/egress) and eth1 (private network, unaddressed); node2/node3 (RHEL9) have enp1s0 (default) and enp8s0 (private, NM profile already ipv4.method=auto with no address)
Set static address 10.50.50.254/24 on node1's eth1

Configured VyOS kea DHCP server (service dhcp-server shared-network-name LAN, subnet 10.50.50.0/24 subnet-id 1, range 10.50.50.100-200, option default-router/name-server, lease 3600) after discovering current syntax from VyOS's own template tree on the node (subnet-parameters/default-router/name-server had to move under 'option', and subnet-id is now required)
Committed and saved the VyOS config so it persists to /config/config.boot
Triggered nmcli con up on node2 and node3's enp8s0 to request DHCP leases from node1; node2 got 10.50.50.101, node3 got 10.50.50.100
Verified bidirectional ping from node1 to both leased addresses over eth1
Captured pre-restart baselines: node1 boot_id + eth1 address + kea-dhcp4 process/socket state; node2/node3 boot_id + leased IP

Restarted node1 via backgrounded 'reboot' (ack returned before disconnect), polled until exec was available again, confirmed changed boot_id (9028a473...->9783f146...), and verified eth1 address and kea-dhcp4 both recovered
Restarted node2, confirmed changed boot_id (910dc564...->69b29666...), and confirmed it re-acquired the same DHCP lease (10.50.50.101) from node1
Restarted node3, confirmed changed boot_id (5f3ce3b8...->bf08027c...), and confirmed it re-acquired the same DHCP lease (10.50.50.100) from node1
Final post-restart connectivity check: node1 pinged both node2 and node3 over the private network successfully

evidence.requirement: node1 runs a DHCP server on the private network shared with node2/node3
evidence.summary: DHCP config committed/saved on node1; kea-dhcp4 process confirmed listening on 10.50.50.254:67 on eth1

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 obtain their private-network address from node1 via DHCP rather than static assignment
evidence.summary: NM profiles for enp8s0 confirmed ipv4.method=auto (DHCP client, not static); after bringing the connection up, node2 leased 10.50.50.101 and node3 leased 10.50.50.100 from node1's server

evidence.requirement: Cross-node connectivity on the private DHCP network works end-to-end
evidence.summary: node1 successfully pinged both node2 (10.50.50.100) and node3 (10.50.50.101) over eth1

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 9028a473... with kea-dhcp4 active captured; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; post-restart boot_id 9783f146... confirms restart; kea-dhcp4 process and eth1 address both recovered

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 910dc564... with lease 10.50.50.101 captured; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 69b29666... confirms restart; enp8s0 re-leased the same DHCP address confirming recovery

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 5f3ce3b8... with lease 10.50.50.100 captured; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id bf08027c... confirms restart; enp8s0 re-leased the same DHCP address confirming recovery
After all three restarts, node1 pinged both node2 and node3 successfully over the private DHCP network
